content.text:
My investigation is complete. The findings:

- **§5.8 (p0367–p0369)** — the only exclusivity covenant in the agreement — binds **Harpoon** not to develop/commercialize Competing Products in the Territory. This runs in our favor.
- **§5.1.3 (p0355–p0356)** grants the exclusive licence **to AbbVie**, including against Harpoon — beneficial to us.
- **§10.4 (p0554–p0556)**, AbbVie's only covenants, contain solely an IP-assignment covenant — no sourcing or non-compete restriction.
- **§7.1.2 (p0429)** confirms the asymmetry expressly: "in the case of Harpoon, its exclusivity obligations hereunder" — i.e., only Harpoon carries exclusivity obligations.
- **§5.4, §5.5, §4.5.1 and §4.5.2** affirmatively preserve AbbVie's freedom to appoint any third-party distributors, co-promoters and third-party manufacturers, and to take a manufacturing technology transfer to a designee of its choice.

No clause obliges AbbVie to source exclusively from Harpoon or restricts AbbVie from developing or procuring alternative BCMA/Delivery System products. This meets the preferred position, so no redline is warranted.

input.quote: 5.8.1 Harpoon shall not, and shall cause its Affiliates not to (a) directly or indirectly, develop, commercialize or otherwise exploit any Competing Product in any country or other jurisdiction in the Territory, or (b) license, authorize, appoint, or otherwise enable any Third Party to directly or indirectly, develop, commercialize or otherwise exploit any Competing Product in any country or other jurisdiction in the Territory
input.rationale: The rule is met at the preferred position: no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation is imposed on AbbVie (our party). The only exclusivity covenant, Section 5.8 (p0367-p0369), binds Harpoon not to develop, commercialize or enable third parties to exploit Competing Products in the Territory, which benefits us and is expressly excluded from flagging by the detection guidance. Likewise, the exclusive licence in Section 5.1.3 (p0355-p0356) is granted to AbbVie, including as against Harpoon and its Affiliates. The asymmetry is confirmed expressly in Section 7.1.2 (p0429), which qualifies each Party's freedom to exploit Joint IP "in the case of Harpoon, its exclusivity obligations hereunder" - i.e. only Harpoon bears exclusivity obligations. AbbVie's sole covenants in Section 10.4 (p0554-p0556) are limited to obtaining IP rights from its Affiliates, Sublicensees and personnel, with no non-compete or sourcing restriction. Our sourcing freedom is affirmatively preserved elsewhere: Section 5.4 (p0360) and 5.5 (p0361) give AbbVie sole discretion to appoint third-party distributors and co-promoters, and Sections 4.5.1-4.5.2 (p0340-p0341) give AbbVie the sole right to Manufacture or have Manufactured Licensed Products and to require a manufacturing technology transfer to a third-party manufacturer of its choice. No provision requires AbbVie to purchase its requirements from Harpoon or restricts AbbVie from developing or procuring alternative BCMA/Delivery System products, so no redline is warranted.
